meta.method: Targeted review of titles, abstracts, publication types and linked notices for all 36 PubMed records in the August Figure 3 ledger, retrieved through Europe PMC. Study-setting labels and summaries were checked against those abstracts. This is not a systematic literature search or a full-text quality assessment. Published correction notices are linked; their full contents have not been assessed.

rows: Acetylated histone H2B was recognized by lupus-associated autoantibodies in patient samples and mouse experiments.
An autoantibody epitope study; it does not establish that acetylation causes lupus.
Family-level audit classification. Coverage describes a PTM family, not disease-specific validation.
Autoantibodies recognized citrullinated tenascin-C in rheumatoid arthritis cohorts and in some samples collected before diagnosis.
Biomarker association and epitope recognition do not establish disease causation.

Experimental mouse models; benefit in patients was not tested.

Two bacterial studies describe AMPylation and UMPylation in infection-related biology.
The studies concern different substrates and organisms. The UMPylation study concerns a bacterial protein, not a host protein; this grouping does not imply a shared disease mechanism.
Family-level audit classification. Coverage describes a PTM family, not disease-specific validation.
A Legionella study reports phosphocholination in host-cell biology.
A mechanistic infection study, not a patient association or a validated clinical target.

A Legionella study examines noncanonical ubiquitin modification during infection.
The phosphoribosyl-linked subtype is distinct from conventional ubiquitination. Family-wide coverage does not establish subtype-specific disease coverage.
